tasks.short: Gather the facts on the performance problem, consult HR, hold the corrective talk, write the warning letter, check it with HR, file it, and follow up.

steps.what: Recreation supervisor gathers incidents, attendance and earlier talks on the worker
Recreation supervisor consults HR about the right disciplinary step
Recreation supervisor takes disciplinary action in a corrective talk with the worker
Recreation supervisor writes the warning letter
Recreation supervisor checks the letter with HR
Recreation supervisor files the signed letter in the personnel file
Recreation supervisor follows up with the worker after the agreed period

tasks.design: The personnel file in the HR system ({HCM}) shows a worker's earlier talks, warnings and attendance on one screen. Warning letters start from HR's templates per disciplinary step with the policy text filled in; the supervisor adds the facts. Once checked with HR, the signed letter is saved in the personnel file with a follow-up reminder. Consulting HR, the talk and follow-up stay with the supervisor; no software rates the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts were gathered from memory and e-mail, and letters written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: HR systems hold personnel files with letter templates and reminders.
tasks.still_hard: A disciplinary talk has to be fair and firm at once.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the reason behind lateness that changes the right response.

evidence.claim: HR systems can hold personnel files with letter templates and follow-up reminders.
AI that evaluates worker performance is high-risk under Annex III point 4(b); here no software evaluates the worker.

assumptions: Boundary: from the performance problem to the follow-up; dismissal procedures are outside.
Input contract: templates kept by HR; attendance from the scheduling tool; fallback is writing from scratch.
Consulting HR, the talk and follow-up do not change.
The worker's time does not change.

incremental.description: Recreation supervisor sets the follow-up reminder.

approvals.approved_version: The letter as checked with HR in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: rare cases with simple letters; high: frequent cases in a large team.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Walk the floor observing workers' appearance and service, give on-the-spot feedback, note observations, and read guest feedback per area.

steps.what: Recreation supervisor observes and evaluates workers' appearance and performance on the floor
Recreation supervisor gives on-the-spot feedback to ensure quality service
Recreation supervisor notes observations on paper
Recreation supervisor reads guest reviews and survey scores

tasks.design: A short area checklist on the supervisor's phone replaces paper notes; it records the state of each area, not scores per worker. Guest reviews and survey scores come together in one dashboard ({BI}) by area and day. Observing workers and giving feedback stay with the supervisor; no camera or software rates staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observations went on paper and guest feedback was read on several sites.
tasks.enabler_now: Phone checklists and review dashboards are common in leisure businesses.
tasks.still_hard: Good service shows in moments a checklist misses.
tasks.human_edge: Praising a worker in front of guests at the right moment.

reach.learn: Whether area feedback reaches the team sooner.

evidence.claim: Phone checklists and dashboards of guest reviews by area are common tools.
Systems that can watch staff attendance or performance need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from service standards to service signals; training workers is outside.
Input contract: standards set by management; reviews from public sites and the guest survey; fallback is paper and separate sites.
Observing and feedback do not change.
Checklists describe areas, not individual workers.

Input contract for s4: reviews pulled from the main public review sites by the dashboard's review connector, and scores from the guest survey tool; sites without a connector, about a fifth, are still read by hand.
research_questions: Do guest scores per area improve?

incremental.description: Recreation supervisor keeps the area checklist current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one small area; high: several areas with many guest reviews.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect visitor, sales and staffing data, record hours, absence and overtime, analyze trends, write the activity report, send it to the manager, and answer questions.

steps.what: Recreation supervisor collects visitor numbers, sales and staff hours from several systems
Recreation supervisor records personnel data such as hours, absence and overtime
Recreation supervisor analyzes operational and personnel trends
Recreation supervisor writes the related activity report

loop.input: The dashboard figures for the period and the supervisor's notes on events.
loop.output: A draft narrative for the activity report.
loop.check: Code checks every number in the text matches the dashboard; the supervisor edits and approves the text.
loop.stop: Stops when numbers match and the supervisor approves, or after two failed redrafts the supervisor writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: The report needs a few lines of explanation each period; a template cannot say why numbers moved.

steps.what: Recreation supervisor e-mails the report to the manager
Recreation supervisor answers the manager's questions about the report

tasks.design: Visitor numbers from ticketing, sales from the till and hours from the scheduling tool ({HCM}) flow into one dashboard ({BI}), and hours, absence and overtime are recorded by time tracking instead of a spreadsheet. A bounded step drafts the report narrative from the dashboard; code checks every number, and the supervisor edits. Once approved, the report goes to the manager. Reading trends stays with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were exported from several systems into spreadsheets and the report written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling tools track time and labour cost against turnover; dashboards join tills and ticketing.
tasks.still_hard: The reasons behind a bad week sit in the supervisor's head.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining that a rainy weekend, not staff, cut sales.

ambition.what: Review labour cost against visitors weekly instead of monthly.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor reads and explains numbers instead of compiling them.

evidence.claim: Shiftbase tracks time and compares labour cost targets against turnover from the till.
A time clock that can watch attendance or performance needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from system exports to questions answered; budget decisions are outside.
Input contract: ticketing, till and scheduling data by integration; fallback is spreadsheets.
Reading trends stays with the supervisor.
Personnel data are shown per team, not to rank workers.
research_questions: How much of the drafted narrative does the supervisor change?

already_counted.description: Recreation supervisor edits and approves the drafted narrative.

incremental.description: Recreation supervisor checks the dashboard feeds after system changes.

approvals.approved_version: The report as edited and approved by the supervisor in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small site with few systems; high: a large site with many data sources.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read trade news, choose courses and trade fairs, register, attend them, share what you learned with the team, and keep certificates.

steps.what: Recreation supervisor reads trade news and newsletters to stay abreast of industry trends
Recreation supervisor chooses courses and trade fairs
Recreation supervisor registers for the chosen events online
Recreation supervisor participates in continuing education, trade fairs and webinars
Recreation supervisor shares what they learned with the team
Recreation supervisor keeps course certificates in a folder

tasks.design: Trade newsletters and association news are filtered into one weekly digest folder instead of a full inbox. Certificates are uploaded to the training record in the HR system ({HCM}) with expiry reminders for licences such as first aid. Choosing, registering for and attending events and sharing with the team stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Trade news arrived scattered in the inbox and certificates sat in a paper folder.
tasks.enabler_now: Mail filters and HR training records with expiry reminders are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Time for courses competes with busy seasons.
tasks.human_edge: Bringing back one idea from a trade fair that the team actually uses.

evidence.claim: HR systems can hold training records with expiry reminders.

assumptions: Boundary: from trade news to certificates kept; the training budget is outside.
Input contract: newsletters chosen by the supervisor; fallback is the inbox and a paper folder.
Attending and sharing do not change.
Course fees are approved as today.
research_questions: Do licence expiries get caught in time?

approvals.approved_version: The events as chosen by the supervisor in s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: little trade reading; high: many newsletters and licences to track.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The recreation supervisor keeps disciplining fairly, observing service, reading trends and learning from the trade; gathering facts, paper notes, spreadsheet compilations and scattered news shrink.
skills_to_grow: Reading dashboards and editing drafted reports
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who spends saved time on the floor with staff and guests.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Entertainment and Recreation Workers, Except Gambling Services
